extracted.intended_audience: Users of Singular (dmodloc.lib) — mathematicians / computational algebraists doing D-module and Weyl-algebra computations
extracted.subtask_description: Documentation for the Singular library dmodloc.lib: procedures to compute closures, ranks, singular loci, polynomial/rational solutions, b-functions, annihilators and related utilities in Weyl algebras / D-modules. Each entry specifies usage, assumptions on the basering/variables, return type, and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: WeylClosure1
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: WeylClosure1(L); L a poly. Assume: The basering is the first Weyl algebra D=K<x,d|dx=xd+1> over a field K of characteristic 0. Return: ideal, the Weyl closure of the principal left ideal generated by L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remarks: The Weyl closure of a left ideal I in D is the intersection of I regarded as left ideal in the rational Weyl algebra K(x)<d> with the polynomial Weyl algebra D. Reference: (Tsa), Algorithm 1.2.4. Note: If printlevel=1, progress debug messages will be printed, if printlevel>=2, all debug messages will be printed. Examples in the manual show invocation and returned ideal generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: holonomicRank
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: holonomicRank(I[,e]); I ideal, e optional int. Assume: basering is the n-th Weyl algebra over a field of characteristic 0 and variables ordered so var(i+n)*var(i)=var(i)*var(i+1)+1. Return: int, the holonomic rank of I (K(x(1..n))-dimension of W/WI); returns -1 if infinite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remarks: If e<>0, std is used for Gröbner basis computations, otherwise (default) slimgb is used. If printlevel=1 prints progress debug messages, if >=2 prints all debug messages. Example: holonomicRank on an ideal annihilating exp(1/f) returns 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: DsingularLocus
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: DsingularLocus(I); I ideal. Assume: basering is the n-th Weyl algebra (char 0) with the usual variable ordering property. Return: ideal describing the singular locus of the D-module D/I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: If printlevel>=1, progress debug messages will be printed, if printlevel>=2, all debug messages will be printed. Example: for I annihilating exp(1/f) the singular locus returned is y^2*z^2-x^3.

rubrics_metrics.name: polSol
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: polSol(I[,w,m]); I ideal, w optional intvec, m optional int. Assume: basering is the n-th Weyl algebra W (char 0) and I is holonomic. Return: ideal, a basis of the polynomial solutions to the given system of linear PDEs encoded via I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remarks: If w is given it should consist of n strictly negative entries; otherwise w defaults to -1:n and is used as weight vector for computing a b-function. If m is provided it is assumed to be the minimal integer root of the b-function of I w.r.t. w (this assumption is not checked). Reference: (OTT), Algorithm 2.4. Note: printlevel controls debug output. Example demonstrating returned polynomial solutions is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: polSolFiniteRank
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: polSolFiniteRank(I[,w]); I ideal, w optional intvec. Assume: basering is n-th Weyl algebra (char 0) and I is of finite holonomic rank. Return: ideal, a basis of the polynomial solutions to the system encoded by I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remarks: If w is given, it should consist of n strictly negative entries; default w = -1:n used as weight vector for b-function computation. Reference: (OTT), Algorithm 2.6. Note: printlevel controls debug output. Example mirrors polSol example but assumes finite rank.

rubrics_metrics.name: ratSol
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ratSol(I); I ideal. Assume: basering is the n-th Weyl algebra W (char 0) and I is holonomic. Return: module, a basis of the rational solutions to the system encoded by I; each entry has two components: numerator and denominator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remarks: Reference: (OTT), Algorithm 3.10. Note: printlevel controls debug output. Example: shows resulting module printed as pairs (numerator, denominator). See polSol / polSolFiniteRank for polynomial-solution-related references.

rubrics_metrics.name: bfctBound
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: bfctBound(I,f[,primdec]); I ideal, f poly, primdec optional string. Assume: basering is the n-th Weyl algebra W (char 0) and I is holonomic. Return: list of roots (type ideal) and multiplicities (intvec) of a multiple of the b-function for f^s*u at a generic root of f (u stands for [1] in D/I).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remarks: Requires computing a primary decomposition in a commutative ring. Optional primdec can be 'GTZ' (Gianni-Trager-Zacharias) or 'SY' (Shimoyama-Yokoyama); default 'GTZ'. Reference: (OTT), Algorithm 3.4. Note: printlevel controls debug output. Cross-references: bernstein, bfct, bfctAnn.

rubrics_metrics.name: annRatSyz
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: annRatSyz(f,g[,db,eng]); f,g polynomials, db,eng optional integers. Assume: basering is commutative and over a field of characteristic 0. Return: ring (a Weyl algebra) containing an ideal 'LD' which is (part of) the annihilator of the rational function g/f in the corresponding Weyl algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remarks: Uses computation of certain syzygies; full annihilator can be obtained by computing the Weyl closure of LD. If db>0, operators of order up to db are considered; otherwise (default) a minimal holonomic solution is computed. If eng<>0, std is used for Gröbner basis computations, otherwise (default) slimgb is used. If printlevel>=1 prints progress messages. Examples show how to compute LD, extend db to get full annihilator, and verify with annRat.

rubrics_metrics.name: dmodGeneralAssumptionCheck
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: dmodGeneralAssumptionCheck(); Return: nothing but checks general assumptions on the basering and prints an error message if any are violated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks: R is the n-th Weyl algebra over a field of characteristic 0; R is not a qring; for all 1<=i<=n the identity var(i+n)*var(i)=var(i)*var(i+1)+1 holds (i.e., variable sequence x(1)..x(n), D(1)..D(n)). Example: when basering is not Weyl it prints '? Basering is not a Weyl algebra' and returns. Use to validate ring before calling other dmodloc functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: extendWeyl
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: extendWeyl(S); S string or list of strings. Assume: basering is the n-th Weyl algebra W (char 0) with standard variable ordering. Return: ring, Weyl algebra extended by variables given by S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: extendWeyl("t") creates new Weyl algebra with t, extendWeyl(list) adds multiple. The resulting ring preserves Weyl noncommutative relations for new D-operators (e.g., Dtt=t*Dt+1). Use setring to activate output ring. Demonstrates variable ordering and name conventions in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: polyVars
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: polyVars(f,v); f poly, v intvec. Return: int, 1 if f contains only variables indexed by v, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: polyVars(y^2+zy, (1,2)) returns 0 (depends on z as well); polyVars with v=(2,3) returns 1. Simple utility for variable-dependence checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: monomialInIdeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: monomialInIdeal(I); I ideal. Return: ideal consisting of all monomials appearing in generators of ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided demonstrating extraction of monomials appearing in generators; useful for analyzing monomial content of generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: vars2pars
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: vars2pars(v); v intvec. Assume: basering is commutative. Return: ring with variables specified by v converted into parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: converting variables to parameters changes coefficient field to QQ(a,b,c) etc. Use setring to switch to returned ring. Demonstrates behavior with different index vectors and resulting ring variable and parameter lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: minIntRoot2
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: minIntRoot2(L); L list. Assume: L is the output of bFactor. Return: int, the minimal integer root in a list of roots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: with polynomial factors containing integer and non-integer roots, minIntRoot2 returns -1. Cross-reference bFactor, minIntRoot, maxIntRoot.

rubrics_metrics.name: maxIntRoot
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: maxIntRoot(L); L list. Assume: L is the output of bFactor. Return: int, the maximal integer root in a list of roots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: returns 2 for sample polynomial. Cross-reference bFactor and related root utilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: dmodAction
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: dmodAction(id,f[,v]); id ideal or poly, f poly, v optional intvec. Assume: If v not given, basering is the n-th Weyl algebra W (char 0) with the usual identity; otherwise v specifies positions of variables forming a Weyl subalgebra. Further assume f does not contain any D(i). Return: same type as id, the result of the natural D-module action of id on f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: The assumptions are not checked. Example: compute annPoly(f) in commutative ring, setring to the Weyl output ring and apply dmodAction(LD,f) to confirm annihilation (outputs zeros). Also applying dmodAction(P,f) where P is an operator returns the action result. Use when evaluating D-module action on polynomials; be careful that function checks are not enforced.

rubrics_metrics.name: dmodActionRat
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: dmodActionRat(id,w); id ideal or poly, w vector. Assume: basering is the n-th Weyl algebra W (char 0). Further assume w has exactly two components, second one non-zero, and w does not contain any D(i). Return: same type as id, the result of the natural D-module action of id on the rational function w[1]/w[2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: demonstrate that x and y act by multiplication and Dx/Dy act by partial derivation on represented rational vector [f,g]. Use to verify LD is annihilator of f/g by applying dmodActionRat(LD,v).

rubrics_metrics.name: simplifyRat
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: simplifyRat(v); v vector. Assume: v has exactly two components, second one non-zero. Return: vector representing simplified rational function v[1]/v[2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Possibly present non-commutative relations of the basering are ignored. Example: simplifyRat([x^2-1,x+1]) returns representation equivalent to [x-1,1]. Use to canonicalize rational vector form before further processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: addRat
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: addRat(v,w); v,w vectors. Assume: both have exactly two components with non-zero denominators. Return: vector representing (v[1]/v[2]) + (w[1]/w[2]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Possibly present non-commutative relations of the basering are ignored. Example: addRat([x,y],[y,x]) yields [x^2+y^2, xy] up to equivalent representation. Use to perform rational arithmetic on 2-component vectors representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: multRat
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: multRat(v,w); v,w vectors. Assume: both have two components, second ones non-zero. Return: vector representing (v[1]/v[2])*(w[1]/w[2]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Possibly present non-commutative relations of the basering are ignored. Example: multRat([x,y],[y,x]) returns [1,1] in example. Use for rational multiplication on vector representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: diffRat
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: diffRat(v,j); v vector, j int. Assume: v has exactly two components, second one non-zero. Return: vector representing derivative of rational function v[1]/v[2] w.r.t. var(j).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Possibly present non-commutative relations of the basering are ignored. Examples show returned vectors correspond to symbolic derivatives; e.g., diffRat([x,y],1) yields [1,y].

rubrics_metrics.name: commRing
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: commRing(); Return: ring — basering without non-commutative relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: makeWeyl(3) then commRing() returns a ring with the same variable names but no Weyl noncommutative relations. Useful to obtain commutative counterpart of a Weyl ring for commutative computations or comparisons. Setting ring r = 0,(x,y),dp; def r2 = commRing(); yields same as r.

rubrics_metrics.name: rightNFWeyl
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: rightNFWeyl(id,k); id ideal or poly, k int. Assume: basering is the n-th Weyl algebra (char 0) with standard variable ordering. Return: same type as id, the right normal form of id with respect to the principal right ideal generated by the k-th variable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: No Gröbner basis computation is used. Examples show computing right normal forms of ideals wrt principal right ideals generated by different variables (x*W, Dx*W, y*W, Dy*W) and for polynomials. Use for fast right-normal-form computations where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: printlevel debug message convention
rubrics_metrics.description: Many procedures document: 'If printlevel=1, progress debug messages will be printed, if printlevel>=2, all the debug messages will be printed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This convention recurs across dmodloc.lib procedures (WeylClosure1, holonomicRank, polSol, polSolFiniteRank, ratSol, bfctBound, annRatSyz, etc.). Users can set printlevel to control verbosity; expected behavior is minimal messages at 1 and full internal debug output at >=2. Use to diagnose or follow long computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: basering and variable-ordering assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Many procedures assume the basering is the n-th Weyl algebra W over a field of characteristic 0 and that for all 1<=i<=n the identity var(i+n)*var(i)=var(i)*var(i+1)+1 holds (i.e., the variable sequence is x(1)..x(n),D(1)..D(n)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These assumptions are explicit prerequisites for correctness of dmodloc procedures (exceptions noted for purely commutative utilities). Use dmodGeneralAssumptionCheck() to verify these conditions; some functions do not check assumptions internally so caller must ensure correct ring/ordering.
